cases.sentence: 13-го июня в 2 часа ночи, государь, призвав к себе Балашева и прочтя ему свое письмо к Наполеону, приказал ему отвезти это письмо и лично передать ___.
cases.explain: «французскому императору» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: At two in the morning of the fourteenth of June, the Emperor, having sent for Balashëv and read him his letter to Napoleon, ordered him to take it and hand it personally to the French Emperor. When dispatching Balashëv, the Emperor repeated to him the words that he would not make peace so long as a single armed enemy remained on Russian soil and told him to transmit those words to Napoleon. Alexander did not insert them in his letter to Napoleon, because with his characteristic tact he felt it would be injudicious to use them at a moment when a last attempt at reconciliation was being made, but he definitely instructed Balashëv to repeat them personally to Napoleon.

cases.sentence: Отправляя Балашева, государь вновь повторил ему слова о том, что он не помирится до тех пор, пока останется хотя один вооруженный неприятель на ___, и приказал непременно передать эти слова Наполеону.
cases.explain: «русской земле» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.

cases.sentence: Французский ___, в малиновом мундире и мохнатой шапке, крикнул на подъезжавшего Балашева, приказывая ему остановиться.
cases.explain: «гусарский унтер-офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: A French noncommissioned officer of hussars, in crimson uniform and a shaggy cap, shouted to the approaching Balashëv to halt. Balashëv did not do so at once, but continued to advance along the road at a walking pace.

cases.sentence: Французский гусарский унтер-офицер, в ___ и мохнатой шапке, крикнул на подъезжавшего Балашева, приказывая ему остановиться.

cases.sentence: Унтер-офицер, нахмурившись и проворчав какое-то ругательство, надвинулся грудью лошади на Балашева, взялся за саблю и грубо крикнул на ___, спрашивая его: глух ли он, что не слышит того, что̀ ему говорят.
cases.explain: «русского генерала» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The noncommissioned officer frowned and, muttering words of abuse, advanced his horse’s chest against Balashëv, put his hand to his saber, and shouted rudely at the Russian general, asking: was he deaf that he did not do as he was told? Balashëv mentioned who he was. The noncommissioned officer began talking with his comrades about regimental matters without looking at the Russian general.

cases.sentence: ___ и трубач и французские гусары молча изредка глядели друг на друга.
cases.explain: «Русские казаки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Balashëv looked around him, awaiting the arrival of an officer from the village. The Russian Cossacks and bugler and the French hussars looked silently at one another from time to time.

cases.sentence: Русские казаки и трубач и ___ молча изредка глядели друг на друга.
cases.explain: «французские гусары» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Balashëv looked around him, awaiting the arrival of an officer from the village. The Russian Cossacks and bugler and the French hussars looked silently at one another from time to time.

cases.sentence: Французский ___, видимо только что с постели, выехал из деревни на красивой, сытой, серой лошади, сопутствуемый двумя гусарами.
cases.explain: «гусарский полковник» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: A French colonel of hussars, who had evidently just left his bed, came riding from the village on a handsome sleek gray horse, accompanied by two hussars. The officer, the soldiers, and their horses all looked smart and well kept.

cases.sentence: ___ с трудом удерживал зевоту, но был учтив и видимо понимал всё значение Балашева.
cases.explain: «Французский полковник» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The French colonel with difficulty repressed a yawn, but was polite and evidently understood Balashëv’s importance. He led him past his soldiers and behind the outposts and told him that his wish to be presented to the Emperor would most likely be satisfied immediately, as the Emperor’s quarters were, he believed, not far off.

cases.sentence: Он провел его мимо своих солдат за цепь и сообщил, что желание его быть представленным императору будет вероятно тотчас же исполнено, так как ___, сколько он знает, находится недалеко.

cases.sentence: Они проехали деревню Рыконты мимо французских ___, часовых и солдат, отдававших честь своему полковнику и с любопытством осматривавших русский мундир, и выехали на другую сторону села.
cases.explain: «гусарских коновязей» — after the preposition «мимо», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: They rode through the village of Rykónty, past tethered French hussar horses, past sentinels and men who saluted their colonel and stared with curiosity at a Russian uniform, and came out at the other end of the village. The colonel said that the commander of the division was a mile and a quarter away and would receive Balashëv and conduct him to his destination.

cases.sentence: Человек этот поехал галопом навстречу Балашеву, блестя и развеваясь на ярком ___ своими перьями, каменьями и золотыми галунами.
cases.explain: «июньском солнце» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: They had hardly ridden up a hill, past a tavern, before they saw a group of horsemen coming toward them. In front of the group, on a black horse with trappings that glittered in the sun, rode a tall man with plumes in his hat and black hair curling down to his shoulders. He wore a red mantle, and stretched his long legs forward in French fashion. This man rode toward Balashëv at a gallop, his plumes flowing and his gems and gold lace glittering in the bright June sunshine.

cases.sentence: Хотя и было совершенно непонятно, почему он был ___, но его называли так, и он сам был убежден в этом, и потому имел более торжественный и важный вид, чем прежде.
cases.explain: «Неаполитанский король» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Balashëv was only two horses’ length from the equestrian with the bracelets, plumes, necklaces, and gold embroidery, who was galloping toward him with a theatrically solemn countenance, when Julner, the French colonel, whispered respectfully: “The King of Naples!” It was, in fact, Murat, now called “King of Naples.” Though it was quite incomprehensible why he should be King of Naples, he was called so, and was himself convinced that he was so, and therefore assumed a more solemn and important air than formerly. He was so sure that he really was the King of Naples that when, on the eve of his departure from that city, while walking through the streets with his wife, some Italians called out to him: “Viva il re!”78 he turned to his wife with a pensive smile and said: “Poor fellows, they don’t know that I am leaving them tomorrow!”

cases.sentence: Увидав ___, он по-королевски, торжественно, откинул назад голову с завитыми по плечи волосами и вопросительно поглядел на французского полковника.
cases.explain: «русского генерала» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: On seeing the Russian general he threw back his head, with its long hair curling to his shoulders, in a majestically royal manner, and looked inquiringly at the French colonel. The colonel respectfully informed His Majesty of Balashëv’s mission, whose name he could not pronounce.

cases.sentence: Как только король начал говорить громко и быстро, всё ___ мгновенно оставило его, и он, сам не замечая, перешел в свойственный ему тон добродушной фамильярности.
cases.explain: «королевское достоинство» — after the preposition «в», the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “De Bal-machève!” said the King (overcoming by his assurance the difficulty that had presented itself to the colonel). “Charmed to make your acquaintance, General!” he added, with a gesture of kingly condescension. As soon as the King began to speak loud and fast his royal dignity instantly forsook him, and without noticing it he passed into his natural tone of good-natured familiarity. He laid his hand on the withers of Balashëv’s horse and said:

cases.sentence: Лицо Мюрата сияло ___ в то время, как он слушал Monsieur de Balachoff.
cases.explain: «глупым довольством» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Murat’s face beamed with stupid satisfaction as he listened to “Monsieur de Bal-machève.” But royauté oblige!79 and he felt it incumbent on him, as a king and an ally, to confer on state affairs with Alexander’s envoy. He dismounted, took Balashëv’s arm, and moving a few steps away from his suite, which waited respectfully, began to pace up and down with him, trying to speak significantly. He referred to the fact that the Emperor Napoleon had resented the demand that he should withdraw his troops from Prussia, especially when that demand became generally known and the dignity of France was thereby offended. Balashëv replied that there was “nothing offensive in the demand, because …” but Murat interrupted him.

cases.sentence: Но royauté oblige:[579] ___ имеет свои обязанности: он чувствовал необходимость переговорить с посланником Александра о государственных делах, как король и союзник.

cases.sentence: И он перешел к расспросам о ___, о его здоровье, и о воспоминаниях веселой забавно проведенного с ним времени в Неаполе.
cases.explain: «великом князе» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Oh, my dear general!” Murat again interrupted him, “with all my heart I wish the Emperors may arrange the affair between them, and that the war begun by no wish of mine may finish as quickly as possible!” said he, in the tone of a servant who wants to remain good friends with another despite a quarrel between their masters. And he went on to inquiries about the Grand Duke and the state of his health, and to reminiscences of the gay and amusing times he had spent with him in Naples. Then suddenly, as if remembering his royal dignity, Murat solemnly drew himself up, assumed the pose in which he had stood at his coronation, and, waving his right arm, said:

cases.sentence: Но вместо ___ с Наполеоном, часовые пехотного корпуса Даву опять так же задержали его у следующего селения как и в передовой цепи, и вызванный адъютант командира корпуса проводил его в деревню к маршалу Даву.
cases.explain: «скорой встречи» — after the preposition «вместо», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Balashëv rode on, supposing from Murat’s words that he would very soon be brought before Napoleon himself. But instead of that, at the next village the sentinels of Davout’s infantry corps detained him as the pickets of the vanguard had done, and an adjutant of the corps commander, who was fetched, conducted him into the village to Marshal Davout.
